title: Lesson 5: Branch Prediction & the Spectre Vulnerability — js-tools
desc: Control hazards and why prediction is necessary, static versus dynamic prediction with 1-bit and 2-bit saturating FSMs plus the Branch History Table, the effective-CPI formula, and how speculative execution opened the Spectre vulnerability. Verified by running a hand-written engine: on a 15-branch nested-loop sequence the 1-bit predictor is right 9/15 (60%) while the 2-bit saturating one reaches 10/15 (66.7%); with 20% branches, a 10% miss rate and a 3-cycle penalty the effective CPI is exactly 1.06. Demo: run both predictors side by side and compute effective CPI interactively.
